question.text: Two identical non-conducting solid spheres of same mass and charge are suspended in air from a common point by two non-conducting, massless strings of same length. At equilibrium, the angle between the strings is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math>. The spheres are now immersed in a dielectric liquid of density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>800</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> and dielectric constant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>21</mn></math>. If the angle between the strings remains the same after the immersion, then

options.text: electric force between the spheres remains unchanged
electric force between the spheres reduces

mass density of the spheres is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>840</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math>
the tension in the strings holding the spheres remains unchanged

As force between two charged bodies doesn't depend upon medium. Hence, the force between them remains same because the distance spheres is same.
